Ranked.title: Ranked mode
Ranked.description: Your real physical and financial level, compared with people your age in Canada and the United States.

intro.what: Take 5 short fitness tests and answer 5 questions about your finances: each pillar gets a level from 1 to 100, and your total level becomes public.
intro.how: Level 87 means you do better than 87% of people your age in Canada and the United States, based on official data (Statistics Canada, Census Bureau, Federal Reserve…). Social and mental stay private. You can re-evaluate every 30 days.

hints.body: Your height and weight give your BMI, which counts for 10% of the physical level. Body type doesn’t change your level.
hints.physical: Do the tests after a 5-minute warm-up, and stop if anything hurts. One test a day, or rest between tests, is fine.
hints.financial: In your country’s currency. These amounts are never shown to other members or sent to Get iT AI in dollars.

form.public: Your physical level, financial level and total level become public: members see them on your profile and next to your name.
form.notice: Your level is calculated automatically from your answers and public data, never by AI. You can correct your answers at your next re-evaluation, or leave Ranked mode at any time: your answers and levels are then deleted.
form.consent: I agree that this information, including financial and health information, is used to calculate my levels, and that these levels are public. My answers are never shown to other members.

reachCm.label: By how many centimeters?
reachCm.hint: Sit on the floor, legs straight in front of you, soles against a wall. Without bending your knees, lean forward slowly with your arms straight and hold for 2 seconds. Measure the gap between your fingertips and your toes (0 if you just touch them).

runMeters.label: Cardio: how far do you go in 12 minutes?
runMeters.hint: Run (or alternate running and walking) as far as you can for 12 minutes, on a track or with a running app. Example: 2.4 km = 2,400 m.

pushUps.label: Strength: how many push-ups can you do in a row?

hint.full: Full push-ups without stopping: body straight, chest down to about a fist from the floor, arms fully extended on the way up. Stop at the first rest or when your form breaks.
hint.knees: Knee push-ups without stopping: body straight from knees to shoulders, chest down to about a fist from the floor, arms fully extended on the way up. Stop at the first rest or when your form breaks.

squats.label: Legs: how many squats can you do in 60 seconds?
squats.hint: Feet shoulder-width apart, go down until your thighs are parallel to the floor (as if sitting on a chair), then stand up with straight legs. Count only full squats.

jumpCm.label: Power: how far can you jump from a standstill?
jumpCm.hint: Standing with feet together behind a line, jump as far forward as you can with both feet, without a run-up. Measure from the line to the nearest heel. Keep the best of 3 tries.

netIncome.label: Your net yearly income
netIncome.hint: What you actually receive after taxes and deductions over the last 12 months (wages, business, investments). Tip: add up your deposited paychecks for a year.

assets.label: Your assets
assets.hint: The total value of what you own: money in the bank, investments (RRSP, TFSA, 401(k)…), home or other properties, business, vehicles.

debts.label: Your debts
debts.hint: The total of what you owe: mortgage, student loans, car loan, credit cards, lines of credit.

monthlyExpenses.label: Your monthly expenses
monthlyExpenses.hint: What you spend on average each month to live (housing, groceries, transportation, bills, going out), not counting your savings or investments.

weeklyHours.label: Your work hours per week
weeklyHours.hint: How many hours you work on average to earn this income (job, business, side gigs), not counting commuting. For the same income, fewer hours means a better level.

results.totalDescription: On average, you do better than {level, number}% of people your age in Canada and the United States.
results.public: These levels are public. Social and mental stay private.
results.factorAge: {factor}: better than {percent} of people your age

method.title: How it’s calculated
method.how: Each result is compared with people your age (and sex, for the fitness tests). Physical: 12-minute run converted to VO2max (FRIEND registry), push-ups (Canadian Society for Exercise Physiology), flexibility (YMCA), squats and standing long jump (estimates). Financial: net income per hour (Census Bureau), net worth (Federal Reserve and Statistics Canada, Canadian amounts at purchasing power parity) and savings rate (Federal Reserve). A pillar’s level is the weighted average of its factors; the total, the average of the two pillars.
method.limits: Limits: squats and the standing long jump have no published adult norms for Canada and the United States (approximate references, marked “Estimate”); the savings rate partly relies on an estimate; Canada’s hourly income uses the US curve; your answers are self-reported, not verified.
